comment: Shared test vectors for the rules.json format. Derived from
docs/specs/RULES-JSON.md, which stays the normative definition.
Two implementations read this file and must agree on every case:
'document' is the PARSED document, never file text: a malformed-JSON case
would pin an engine-specific parser message that the two runtimes cannot
agree on. Whole-file rejection on the first error is what 'message' pins.
Adding a validation rule means adding a case here in the same commit.

comment: The expected rectangles are hardcoded known-good values, pinned to the
same numbers as the Rust unit tests in cli/src/geometry.rs. Never
recompute them from an implementation's own formula.
The sample workarea (0, 27, 1920, 1053) is a 1920x1080 screen minus the

place.name: pixels and keywords mix, flush with the bottom right
a negative X is a coordinate
left and top are the workarea origin, not the screen origin
a window wider than the workarea goes negative rather than clamping
centring a window wider than the workarea goes negative
a percentage above 100 is not clamped
the size is resolved before the alignment that uses it

place_invalid.name: a percent sign with no digits
a space before the percent sign
an inherited prototype key is not a size token

tile.comment: width 1001 is not divisible by 4: cells floor to 250 and a 1px remainder is left at the right edge
the workarea origin offsets every cell

center.name: a frame larger than the workarea goes negative

comment: The match predicate, shared by the D-Bus selector and rules.json.
'window' is the duck-typed window the predicate is applied to.

cases.name: class does not match a substring
title does not match a substring

no_predicate.name: an empty substring would match every window
pid zero is the unknown-pid sentinel
